examples.ko: 옆 가게가 무엇을 파는지 염탐하러 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to snoop around and see what the shop next door sells.
I heard he got caught spying on a rival company.
Don't snoop into other people's business.
The child eavesdropped on the adults' talk through the crack in the door.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 우리 계획을 염탐하고 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems that person is snooping on our plans.

examples.ko: 몰래 염탐해서 알아낸 정보라서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: The information was found out by secretly snooping, so it is hard to trust.

explain: 상대가 모르게 몰래 사정을 알아보는 것이에요. 그냥 '엿보다'는 보는 행동에 가깝고, '염탐하다'는 정보를 알아내려는 목적이 있어요. 가벼운 농담으로 '친구 소개팅을 염탐했다'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling secretly snooped around my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 모르게 한다는 뜻이 이미 있지만, '몰래'를 붙여 더 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The secrecy is already implied, but adding 몰래 makes it clearer.

phrases.en: I went to check out the new cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보를 알아내려고 간다는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state that you go in order to find things out.

phrases.en: I peeked into the room through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염탐하다보다 보는 행동에 가까운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Closer to the act of looking than 염탐하다 is.

explain_en: It means secretly finding out someone's situation without them knowing. '엿보다' is closer to just peeking, while '염탐하다' has the purpose of gathering information. It can also be used jokingly, as in 'I snooped on my friend's blind date'.

examples.en: We took shelter in a cave to avoid the typhoon.

examples.ko: 고양이가 차 밑에 은신해서 찾기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The cat was hiding under a car, so it was hard to find.

examples.ko: 아이들은 나무 뒤에 은신하고 숨바꼭질을 했어요.
examples.en: The kids hid behind a tree and played hide-and-seek.
Wild animals hide in the forest during the day.

examples.ko: 비가 쏟아져서 은신할 곳을 빨리 찾아야 했어요.
examples.en: It poured, so we had to quickly find a place to take cover.
Rabbits are used to hiding in the grass.

explain: '숨다'는 어디서나 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, '은신하다'는 위험을 피해 몸을 숨긴다는 느낌이 더 강하고 딱딱해요. 대화에서는 '숨다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 글이나 뉴스에서 '은신처'와 함께 자주 나와요. 보통 '~에 은신하다'처럼 장소 뒤에 '에'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: The police found the criminal's hideout.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨어 있는 장소를 말하고, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a hiding place and often appears in the news.

phrases.example: 그는 산속에 몇 달 동안 은신해 있었어요.
phrases.en: He stayed hidden in the mountains for several months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨어서 한동안 머무는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for staying in hiding for some time.

phrases.en: The child hid behind the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은신하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 'eunsinhada' and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: '숨다' is the easy, all-purpose word, while '은신하다' feels more stiff and suggests hiding the body to avoid danger. In conversation '숨다' is used more, and '은신하다' appears in writing and news along with '은신처'. It usually takes '에' after the place, as in '~에 은신하다'.

t90.ax: Rabbits are used to hiding in the grass.

en: to destroy oneself; to ruin oneself

examples.en: He got greedy and ended up ruining himself.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 무리한 투자 때문에 자멸하고 말았어요.
examples.en: That company ruined itself because of reckless investments.

examples.ko: 서로 싸우기만 하면 팀이 자멸할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you only fight each other, the team can destroy itself.
If you keep lying, you'll ruin yourself someday.

examples.ko: 자멸하는 길인 줄 알면서도 그는 멈추지 않았어요.
examples.en: He knew it was a path to self-ruin, but he didn't stop.

examples.ko: 자멸하지 않으려면 지금 방식을 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid ruining yourselves, you have to change your current approach.

explain: 남 때문이 아니라 자기 잘못이나 내부 문제 때문에 무너질 때 써요. '망하다'는 원인과 상관없이 쓰지만 '자멸하다'는 스스로 불러온 결과라는 느낌이 강해요. 회사, 팀, 계획 같은 큰 일에 많이 어울려요.

phrases.en: The team ended up destroying itself by fighting each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 말다'를 붙이면 안타까운 결과로 끝났다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 말다 gives a feeling of regret that it ended that way.

phrases.en: Holding on with lies is a path to self-destruction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 망하는 방향으로 가는 행동을 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn about actions that lead toward one's own ruin.

phrases.en: If you push too hard, you can ruin yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하지 않으면 스스로 무너질 수 있다는 가능성을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses the possibility of collapsing by one's own doing if one isn't careful.

explain_en: It is used when something falls apart because of its own mistakes or internal problems, not because of others. '망하다' can be used for any cause, but '자멸하다' strongly suggests it was self-inflicted. It fits big things like companies, teams and plans.

en: change of direction, stance or field (e.g. switching sports or beliefs)

examples.ko: 그 선수는 야구에서 축구로 전향을 결심했어요.
examples.en: That athlete decided to switch from baseball to soccer.
Everyone was surprised by the sudden change of course.
Even after the switch, they keep practicing hard.
The coach allowed the player to switch positions.
A reporter asked why they had made the switch.
Changing course is not an easy decision.

explain: 전향은 지금까지 하던 방향이나 입장을 다른 쪽으로 바꾸는 거예요. 스포츠에서는 종목이나 포지션을 바꿀 때, 뉴스에서는 생각이나 입장을 바꿀 때 주로 써요. 일상에서 단순히 마음을 바꿀 때는 '마음이 바뀌다'를 써요.

phrases.en: That politician declared a change of stance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입장을 바꾼다고 공개적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when publicly announcing a change of stance.

phrases.example: 종목 전향 후 첫 경기에서 이겼어요.
phrases.en: I won my first match after switching sports.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠에서 하던 종목을 바꾸는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to switching the sport one plays.

phrases.en: After the switch, he became more famous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바꾼 뒤의 변화를 말할 때 '후'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 후 to talk about what changed after the switch.

explain_en: 전향 is a shift away from the direction or stance one held before. In sports it means changing events or positions; in the news it means changing views. For simply changing your mind in daily life, say 마음이 바뀌다.

en: sharply; with a sudden hard thrust

examples.ko: 화가 나서 문을 콱 닫아 버렸어요.
examples.en: I got angry and slammed the door shut.
I drove the nail firmly into the wall.

examples.ko: 목이 콱 막혀서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: My throat choked up and I couldn't speak.
The baby grabbed my finger tightly.

examples.ko: 그냥 콱 사표를 내 버리고 싶어요.
examples.en: I just want to hand in my resignation and be done with it.
The puppy bit my hand hard.

explain: 갑자기 세게 박히거나 막히는 느낌이에요. '꽉'은 단단히 쥐거나 가득 찬 느낌이 중심이고, '콱'은 힘이 순간적으로 확 들어가는 느낌이 강해요. '콱 막히다', '콱 닫다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I felt so stifled that my breath caught sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 갑자기 세게 막히는 느낌을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses something suddenly and sharply getting blocked.

phrases.en: I jabbed the potato hard with a fork.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 순간적으로 세게 주어 찌르는 동작에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a quick, forceful jab.

phrases.en: The nail was driven hard into the wood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 깊고 단단하게 박힌 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something lodged deep and firm.

explain_en: It conveys something suddenly and forcefully lodging in or getting blocked. '꽉' centers on gripping firmly or being packed full, while '콱' stresses a burst of force at one moment. It is common in '콱 막히다' and '콱 닫다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 내 의견을 완전히 깔아뭉갰어요.
examples.en: He completely brushed aside my opinion.

examples.ko: 선배가 후배의 아이디어를 깔아뭉개면 안 돼요.
examples.en: A senior shouldn't trample on a junior's ideas.

examples.ko: 회사가 직원들의 요구를 계속 깔아뭉개고 있어요.
examples.en: The company keeps ignoring the employees' demands.

examples.ko: 아이들이 꽃밭을 깔아뭉개서 정원이 엉망이 됐어요.
examples.en: The kids trampled the flower bed, and the garden turned into a mess.

examples.ko: 남의 노력을 깔아뭉개는 말은 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't say things that trample on other people's efforts.

examples.ko: 민원을 깔아뭉개지 말고 제대로 처리해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't brush off the complaint and handle it properly.

explain: 발로 밟아 뭉개는 동작에도 쓰지만, 요즘은 남의 의견이나 요구를 일부러 무시하고 짓밟을 때 더 자주 들려요. 그냥 '무시하다'보다 더 세고 화난 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Please don't trample on other people's efforts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 남의 노력이나 의견을 무시하지 말라고 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to firmly tell someone not to disregard others' efforts or opinions.

phrases.example: 회사가 직원들의 요구를 깔아뭉개서 모두 화가 났어요.
phrases.en: The company ignored the employees' demands, so everyone was angry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요구', '의견', '제안' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 일부러 무시하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Goes with words like demands, opinions, or proposals, and implies deliberate disregard.

phrases.en: I was upset because my friend ignored what I said.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일반적이고 부드러운 말이에요. '깔아뭉개다'는 짓밟듯이 훨씬 세게 무시하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general, milder word. '깔아뭉개다' feels much harsher, like trampling.

explain_en: It can describe physically stamping something flat, but it is often heard for deliberately ignoring and crushing someone's opinion or request. It feels stronger and angrier than plain '무시하다'.

t90.ax: He completely brushed aside my opinion.

examples.ko: 친구가 계속 농지거리를 해서 웃음이 났어요.
examples.en: My friend kept joking around, and it made me laugh.
This is no time for joking around.
He jokes around so much that it makes me uncomfortable.
I eased the mood with some banter during the meeting.
Stop joking and let's talk seriously.
His tone was mixed with banter, so I didn't get angry.

explain: '농담'보다 조금 점잖지 못하고 장난이 지나친 말이라는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 '농지거리를 하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일상에서는 가볍게 '농담'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I played around joking with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어를 가장 흔한 꼴로 쓴 말로, 장난이 좀 지나친 농담을 주고받는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common form of the headword, with the feel of exchanging rather rowdy jokes.

phrases.en: It's meeting time, so please stop the banter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 장난스러운 말을 그만두게 할 때 쓰는 존댓말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to stop joking around.

phrases.example: 농담이라고 해도 그 말은 너무 심했어요.
phrases.en: Even if it was a joke, that was too harsh.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농지거리보다 가볍고 점잖은 말이라서 일상에서는 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and more polite than 농지거리, so it is used more in daily conversation.

explain_en: Compared with '농담' (a joke), it feels a bit less decent, like horseplay that goes too far. It mostly appears as '농지거리를 하다', and in daily talk people simply say '농담'.

en: to be pestered; to be hassled

examples.ko: 하루 종일 상사에게 들볶여서 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: I was hounded by my boss all day, so I'm exhausted.
I get nagged by my parents every exam season.

examples.ko: 회의에서 들볶이는 날은 밥도 맛이 없어요.
examples.en: On days when I get hassled in meetings, even food tastes bad.
Yesterday I was pestered by the kids.

examples.ko: 이렇게 계속 들볶이면 아무것도 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: If I keep getting hassled like this, I can't do anything.
I was pressed so hard about the deadline yesterday that I finally blew up.

explain: '들볶다'의 피동형으로, 누군가의 잔소리나 재촉에 시달릴 때 써요. 사람에게는 '~에게/한테 들볶이다'로 말하고, 일에 시달릴 때는 '마감에 들볶이다'처럼 '에'를 쓰기도 해요. '시달리다'와 비슷하지만 들볶이다는 계속 닦달당하는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I was nagged all day long, so I'm exhausted.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어서'로 이어서 시달린 뒤의 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-아/어서' form links the nagging to its outcome.

phrases.en: I'm swamped with work these days and can't rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들볶이다'보다 넓게 힘든 일이나 고통에 괴로울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than '들볶이다'; used for being troubled by any hardship.

phrases.en: I'm not nagged by my parents anymore, so it's comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 표현을 붙여서 잔소리에서 벗어난 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form describes being free from nagging.

explain_en: It is the passive form of '들볶다', used when you suffer under someone's nagging or pushing. For a person, say '~에게/한테 들볶이다'; for work pressure, '에' works too, as in '마감에 들볶이다'. It is close to '시달리다' but stronger in the feeling of being constantly pressed.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어릴 때부터 동네 망나니로 소문났어요.
examples.en: He has been known as the neighborhood hellion since he was a kid.

examples.ko: 아들이 망나니처럼 굴어서 부모님 속이 타요.
examples.en: Their son behaves like a ruffian, and his parents are worried sick.
Stop behaving like a ruffian now.

examples.ko: 한때 망나니였던 그가 의사가 됐다니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't believe he became a doctor after being such a hellion.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 소리를 지르다니 완전 망나니네요.
examples.en: Shouting in the middle of a meeting, he's a real brute.
I heard that troublemaker caused another incident.

explain: 말과 행동이 거칠고 막된 사람을 욕할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 아주 심한 말이 되니 조심하세요. 가볍게 장난치는 아이에게는 '말썽꾸러기'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 하는 짓이 망나니 같아요.
phrases.en: That person acts like a ruffian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동이 거칠고 막된 사람을 비난할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone whose behavior is rough and unruly.

phrases.example: 그는 젊을 때 망나니짓을 많이 했어요.
phrases.en: He did a lot of wild, reckless things when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막되고 난폭한 행동을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to wild and violent behavior.

phrases.en: My son is a troublemaker who plays a lot of pranks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '망나니'보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌으로 아이에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and more affectionate than 망나니, used for children.

explain_en: It is a word used to condemn someone whose speech and behavior are rough and unruly. Saying it directly to a person is very harsh, so be careful. For a child who is just playfully naughty, people say '말썽꾸러기' instead.

examples.en: That incident tarnished the school's name.
Be careful not to disgrace the family's name.

examples.ko: 거짓말을 해서 부모님 얼굴에 먹칠하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to bring shame on my parents by lying.
The player who tarnished the team's honor apologized.
The child smeared ink on the wall for fun.
I'm so sorry for disgracing your name.

explain: 실제로 먹을 바르는 뜻보다 '얼굴에 먹칠하다', '명예에 먹칠하다'처럼 체면이나 이름을 더럽힌다는 비유로 훨씬 많이 써요. 주로 자기 행동 때문에 가족이나 단체를 부끄럽게 만들 때 나와요.

phrases.en: His behavior brought shame on his family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 체면이나 명예를 크게 해칠 때 쓰는 부정적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative expression for seriously damaging someone's reputation or honor.
phrases.en_equiv: drag someone's name through the mud

explain_en: Much more often than the literal act of applying ink, it is used figuratively for dirtying someone's face or name, as in '얼굴에 먹칠하다' and '명예에 먹칠하다'. It mostly appears when your actions bring shame on your family or group.

examples.en: He slandered and schemed against his rival to take the position.

examples.ko: 남을 모략한 사람은 결국 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: A person who schemes against others eventually loses trust.

examples.ko: 소문을 퍼뜨려 동료를 모략하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not spread rumors to scheme against a colleague.
Evidence came out that they plotted against me.
The courtier who tried to plot against the queen was caught.

examples.ko: 친구를 모략할 생각은 한 번도 없었어요.
examples.en: I never once thought of scheming against my friend.

explain: '누구를 모략하다'처럼 사람을 목적어로 받아서, 거짓 소문이나 꾸민 일로 남을 곤경에 빠뜨릴 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '험담하다', '누명을 씌우다'가 더 흔하게 들려요. 글이나 역사 이야기에서 더 잘 어울리는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 저를 모략한 사람이 누구인지 알고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to know who plotted against me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모략하다'를 관형형으로 써서 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used to describe a person who plotted against someone.

phrases.en: He got a job by plotting against his friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모략한 일이 어떤 결과의 방법이 되었음을 연결해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form showing the plotting was the means to a result.

phrases.en: Please don't plot against others without grounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 해치는 일을 하지 말라고 존댓말로 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request not to scheme against others.

explain_en: It takes a person as its object, as in '누구를 모략하다', and means to put someone in trouble with false rumors or fabricated schemes. In daily conversation '험담하다' or '누명을 씌우다' is more common. It fits writing and historical stories better.

en: to be vulgar; to be coarse; to be indecent

examples.ko: 상스러운 말은 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to use vulgar language.
That person's way of speaking is a bit coarse.
Don't talk crudely in front of the child.
I was careful because I was afraid of being called vulgar.

examples.ko: 상스럽지 않게 웃는 법을 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to learn how to laugh without seeming coarse.
The crude joke made the mood awkward.

explain: 말, 말투, 행동이 점잖지 않고 거칠 때 써요. 욕을 직접 말하지 않고 '상스러운 말'이라고 돌려 말할 때도 많아요. 반대 느낌의 말로는 '점잖다', '우아하다'가 있고, ㅂ 불규칙이라 '상스러워요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 아이 앞에서 상스러운 말은 하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't use vulgar language in front of children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 욕을 돌려 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing; also a roundabout way to refer to swearing.

phrases.en: He talks coarsely when he gets angry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하는 방식이 거칠다는 뜻으로 부사형을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes a rough manner of speaking.

phrases.en: That joke isn't vulgar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 거칠지 않고 괜찮다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something isn't crude.

explain_en: It describes speech, manner or behavior that is not refined and feels rough. People often say '상스러운 말' to refer to swearing indirectly. Words with the opposite feeling are '점잖다' and '우아하다', and it is ㅂ-irregular, becoming '상스러워요'.

t90.ax: The crude joke made the mood awkward.

examples.ko: 그는 힘든 일에 늘 솔선해서 나서요.
examples.en: He always steps up first for hard work.
Many people take the lead in cleaning the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 아무도 안 하길래 제가 솔선해 봤어요.
examples.en: Since nobody was doing it, I took the lead and tried.
If you take the lead, other people help too.
The chairman took the lead and started donating.
The meeting dragged on because nobody would take the lead.

explain: 남보다 먼저 나서서 한다는 점이 중요해요. '솔선해서 ~하다' 형태로 자주 쓰고, 윗사람에게는 '솔선하시다'처럼 높여요. 모범까지 강조하면 '솔선수범하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: He takes the lead even in tough chores.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~을 솔선해서 하다' 형태로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern: 'do something taking the lead'.
phrases.en_equiv: to do it taking the lead

phrases.en: The employees respect the boss who always takes the lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람을 높여서 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form used for someone senior.

phrases.example: 회의 준비는 민수 씨가 먼저 나섰어요.
phrases.en: Minsu stepped up first to prepare the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 일상적으로 쓰는 비슷한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday expression with a similar meaning.

explain_en: The key point is acting before others do. It is often used as '솔선해서 ~하다', and for elders you say '솔선하시다'. If you want to stress setting an example, use '솔선수범하다'.

t90.ax: He always steps up first for hard work.

examples.ko: 손님을 푸대접하는 가게는 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: A shop that treats its customers poorly won't last long.
Please don't treat people badly just because they are new.
Even though it's a country restaurant, they don't treat guests poorly.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 혼자 온 손님을 푸대접해서 다시 안 가요.
examples.en: That restaurant treats solo diners badly, so I don't go back.

examples.ko: 가족이라고 해서 푸대접해도 되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being family doesn't mean you can treat them badly.

examples.ko: 그분은 어려운 사람들을 절대 푸대접하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He never treated people in need with disrespect.

explain: 반대말은 '극진히 대접하다'예요. 비슷한 말 '홀대하다'는 조금 더 글에서 많이 보여요. 명사 '푸대접'과 함께 '푸대접을 받다'라고 하면 '대우를 못 받다'라는 말이 돼요.

phrases.example: 그 식당에서 푸대접을 받아서 기분이 나빴어요.
phrases.en: I was treated poorly at that restaurant, so I felt bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대접받는 쪽의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person treated badly.

phrases.en: I was treated poorly for being a foreigner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'보다 억울한 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a stronger sense of being wronged than '받다'.

phrases.en: You shouldn't treat your guests coldly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 글에서 더 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and more common in writing.

explain_en: The opposite is '극진히 대접하다' (to treat with great hospitality). A similar word, '홀대하다', appears a bit more in writing. With the noun, '푸대접을 받다' means to be treated poorly.

t90.ax: He never treated people in need with disrespect.

examples.ko: 요즘 살림이 궁색해서 여행은 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: Money is tight these days, so I can't even dream of traveling.
Your reason for being late is really lame.
Please don't make such a weak excuse.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 집안 형편이 궁색했지만 늘 행복했어요.
examples.en: Our family was poor when I was little, but I was always happy.

examples.ko: 돈은 없어도 궁색하게 보이고 싶지는 않아요.
examples.en: Even if I have no money, I don't want to look needy.
My pay was cut, so life is getting harder and harder.

explain: '가난하다'가 재산이 없는 상태를 말한다면, '궁색하다'는 돈이 모자라 쪼들리는 모습에도 쓰고 말이나 변명이 떳떳하지 못하고 부족할 때도 써요. 변명이나 이유를 말할 때는 '궁색한 변명'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I don't want to hear a lame excuse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유가 떳떳하지 못하고 부족할 때 '변명' 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before 변명 for an excuse that is weak and unconvincing.

phrases.example: 낡은 가방 때문에 좀 궁색해 보여요.
phrases.en: The worn bag makes me look a bit needy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 넉넉하지 않아 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one's look seems short of means.

phrases.en: I get a salary now, so I'm not hard up anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 형편이 어렵지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative means one's finances are no longer tight.

explain_en: '가난하다' describes simply having little money, while '궁색하다' also shows a pinched, strained look, and it is used for weak, unconvincing words or excuses. For excuses and reasons, people often say '궁색한 변명'.
